h1: Electrical Panel Upgrades and Replacement in Broward County
intro: When your electrical panel is worn out or unsafe, everything downstream of it is at risk. A failing panel shows it: breakers that trip repeatedly, a burning smell, scorch marks, or lights that dim when the AC starts. Sometimes the first sign is a letter from your insurer, since South Florida carriers now drop homes with obsolete panels. We replace it once and handle the permit and inspector for you.

definition.heading: What an electrical panel upgrade is
definition.body: A panel upgrade removes your old load center and installs a modern one built to current code. The panel divides utility power into the circuits that feed your property. Older ones wear out, run short on space, or use equipment insurers no longer accept. The result is a service that is safe, current, and insurable again.

symptoms.title: Your insurer or inspector flagged it
symptoms.body: Your carrier sent a notice, or a 4-point inspection called out the panel. In South Florida this is the most common reason people call us, and coverage often will not renew until the equipment meets a modern standard.

symptoms.title: Breakers trip for no clear reason
symptoms.body: Breakers trip often, or one refuses to reset. A breaker that will not hold is telling you something downstream is wrong, or the breaker itself is worn out.

symptoms.title: You smell burning or see scorch marks
symptoms.body: A burning smell, scorch marks, or discoloration around the panel cover means heat where there should be none. It usually points to a failing connection and deserves a look before it gets worse.

symptoms.title: You have a fuse box or a flagged brand
symptoms.body: You still have an old fuse box, or a panel from a brand insurers flag, such as Zinsco or Federal Pacific. The name alone, not a symptom, is often what an inspector reacts to.

localSections.heading: South Florida homes and the panels inside them
localSections.body: Broward County housing was built across many decades, and every era left its own electrical fingerprint. Older homes still carry fuse boxes or brands insurers no longer accept. The climate does not help: heat, humidity, and salt air corrode the lugs and bus bars inside a panel, so equipment here ages faster than it would in a cooler, drier place.

localSections.heading: Why carriers are driving so many upgrades
localSections.body: The South Florida insurance market has tightened, and outdated electrical equipment is one of the first things carriers look at. A 4-point inspection covers the roof, plumbing, HVAC, and electrical, and an obsolete panel is a common reason the electrical section fails. The fix is straightforward: replace the panel with a modern one, pass inspection, and the objection goes away.

guide.title: The complete guide to upgrading your electrical panel in South Florida

sections.heading: What a panel upgrade actually is
sections.body: Your electrical panel is where power from the utility enters and divides into the circuits that feed your property. People call it the panel, breaker box, load center, or fuse box. An upgrade removes the old equipment and installs a modern replacement built to current code, along with its breakers and grounding. The result is a panel sized for how you use power, with breakers that trip when they should.

sections.heading: The panels insurers flag: Zinsco, Federal Pacific, and old fuse boxes
sections.body: A handful of older panel types come up repeatedly when carriers and 4-point inspections flag a home. Zinsco and Federal Pacific panels, whose breakers are often labeled Stab-Lok, are obsolete brands whose breakers can fail to trip under a fault. Old fuse boxes are the other common flag. Genuine parts are hard to source, so replacement is the honest answer, and a modern, code-compliant panel removes the brand objection.

sections.heading: How to choose the right contractor
sections.body: A panel sits at the center of your home's safety, so the contractor matters. Ghost Crown Electric is a Florida Certified Electrical Contractor and a Broward County Master Electrician, with 286 permitted projects on public record. Our in-house crew handles the replacement in one visit, pulls the permit, and meets the inspector in person. If your panel is safe and current, we will tell you that and leave it alone.

faqs.question: My insurance company flagged my panel. What now?
faqs.answer: Send us the notice or the 4-point report and we will read it with you. In most cases the fix is a modern, code-compliant panel that passes inspection. We assess the service in person, pull the permit, and meet the inspector so your carrier's objection goes away.

faqs.question: I have a Zinsco or Federal Pacific panel. Do I have to replace it?
faqs.answer: In most cases, yes. These are obsolete brands with a documented history of breakers that can fail to trip under a fault, and genuine parts are hard to source, so a real repair is rarely practical. That said, if your panel is a safe, current brand with room to spare, we will not talk you into replacing it.

faqs.question: Do I really need a permit for this?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you want one. A permit puts a licensed contractor and a county inspector between you and a costly mistake, and it documents that the work meets current code. We pull the permit, schedule the inspection, and meet the inspector on site.

faqs.question: Will my power be off during the work?
faqs.answer: For part of the day, yes, since replacing a panel means safely interrupting the power that feeds it. We tell you honestly ahead of time what to expect so you can plan around it, and because our in-house crew does this constantly, it is a focused, one-visit job.
